acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core publicly exports distinct Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick types; assigning any one branded type to another fails the compile-time type test.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/index.mts exports all five APIs. numeric.mts uses separate unique-symbol brands, and numeric.type-test.mts asserts all directed cross-brand combinations plus primitive-to-brand non-assignability.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate have bigint as their underlying representation, while Tick has number as its underlying representation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: numeric.mts defines the four fixed-point types as intersections with bigint and Tick as an intersection with number; constructors return the corresponding primitives.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Tick constructor accepts exactly safe integers in the inclusive range [Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] and rejects fractional numbers, NaN, infinities, and values outside that range.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Tick uses Number.isSafeInteger after a primitive-type guard. Tests cover both boundaries, adjacent out-of-range values, positive and negative fractions, NaN, and both infinities.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Runtime constructors reject values whose primitive type does not match the represented type.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The bigint constructors use an explicit typeof value !== 'bigint' guard, while Tick first requires typeof value === 'number'. Runtime tests exercise representative incorrect primitive types.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core publicly exports the required bigint scale constants without floating-point conversion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: index.mts re-exports QUANTITY_SCALE, PRICE_SCALE, and RATE_SCALE; numeric.mts initializes them directly as 100_000_000n, 10_000n, and 100_000_000n.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No production implementation uses forbidden nondeterministic facilities, floating-point arithmetic, or mutable global state.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The production diff uses bigint literals, primitive checks, Number.isSafeInteger, immutable module bindings, and error construction only. Automated lint exited successfully.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The repository compile, lint, test, and dependency-boundary commands all exit successfully.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Automated validation proves lint and 149 tests pass, but contains no compile or dependency-boundary command. The Implementer report asserts those commands passed without corresponding captured validation output.

findings.evidence: The Implementer report explicitly states that ADR-001 constrains Tick to non-negative values while the task and ADR-003 require the full signed safe-integer range. The candidate accepts and tests negative Tick values, no ADR was updated, and no blocker record is identified. CICLO_SPEC §19 requires contradictions to be recorded rather than silently choosing one side.
findings.required_change: Create the blocker record required by CICLO_SPEC §19 for the ADR-001 versus ADR-003/task Tick-range contradiction and obtain the prescribed resolution before implementing behavior that depends on it. Then align the constructor and tests with that authoritative resolution.
findings.title: Tick specification contradiction was resolved without a blocker record

findings.evidence: The automated output runs npm ci, git diff --check, lint, and test only. It explicitly warns that no typecheck or build script exists and contains no npm run compile or npm run boundary result, although both are required acceptance validations. This is especially material because nominal isolation is enforced only at TypeScript compilation time.
findings.required_change: Run the repository's exact compile and dependency-boundary commands against the final candidate and provide successful captured outputs. Ensure compilation includes numeric.type-test.mts so the negative type assertions are actually enforced.
findings.title: Mandatory compile and dependency-boundary validation evidence is absent

invariants_checked: Distinct unique-symbol brands prevent cross-brand structural assignment
Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate remain bigint-backed
Tick is number-backed and guarded by Number.isSafeInteger
Scale constants use direct bigint literals
CanonicalEncoder files and vectors are unchanged by the candidate diff
Core production code introduces no higher-layer imports
No forbidden nondeterministic API or mutable global state appears in the production diff
Strict compiler settings are not modified by the candidate
risks: Without compiler validation, the compile-time nominal guarantees may not be exercised by canonical validation.
Accepting signed negative Tick values before resolving the recorded ADR conflict could establish behavior contrary to the governing specification.
payload.summary: The implementation appears to satisfy the task-level numeric API requirements, but it cannot become canonical because the reported ADR-001/ADR-003 Tick-range contradiction was resolved without the blocker process required by CICLO_SPEC §19, and automated evidence omits the mandatory compile and dependency-boundary validations.
